126 |         calibrated using testing data, for each `cv` fold. The final estimator
127 |         is an ensemble of `n_cv` fitted classifer and calibrator pairs, where
128 |         `n_cv` is the number of cross-validation folds. The output is the
129 |         average predicted probabilities of all pairs.
130 | 
131 |         If `False`, `cv` is used to compute unbiased predictions, via
132 |         :func:`~sklearn.model_selection.cross_val_predict`, which are then
133 |         used for calibration. At prediction time, the classifier used is the
134 |         `base_estimator` trained on all the data.
135 |         Note that this method is also internally implemented  in
136 |         :mod:`sklearn.svm` estimators with the `probabilities=True` parameter.
137 | 
138 |         .. versionadded:: 0.24
139 | 
140 |     Attributes
141 |     ----------
142 |     classes_ : ndarray of shape (n_classes,)
143 |         The class labels.
144 | 
145 |     n_features_in_ : int
146 |         Number of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if the
147 |         underlying base_estimator exposes such an attribute when fit.
148 | 
149 |         .. versionadded:: 0.24
150 | 
151 |     feature_names_in_ : ndarray of shape (`n_features_in_`,)
152 |         Names of features seen during :term:`fit`. Only defined if the
153 |         underlying base_estimator exposes such an attribute when fit.
154 | 
155 |         .. versionadded:: 1.0
156 | 
157 |     calibrated_classifiers_ : list (len() equal to cv or 1 if `cv="prefit"` \
158 |             or `ensemble=False`)
159 |         The list of classifier and calibrator pairs.
160 | 
161 |         - When `cv="prefit"`, the fitted `base_estimator` and fitted
162 |           calibrator.
163 |         - When `cv` is not "prefit" and `ensemble=True`, `n_cv` fitted
164 |           `base_estimator` and calibrator pairs. `n_cv` is the number of
165 |           cross-validation folds.
166 |         - When `cv` is not "prefit" and `ensemble=False`, the `base_estimator`,
167 |           fitted on all the data, and fitted calibrator.
168 | 
169 |         .. versionchanged:: 0.24
170 |             Single calibrated classifier case when `ensemble=False`.
171 | 
172 |     Examples
173 |     --------
174 |     >>> from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
175 |     >>> from sklearn.naive_bayes import GaussianNB
176 |     >>> from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV
177 |     >>> X, y = make_classification(n_samples=100, n_features=2,
178 |     ...                            n_redundant=0, random_state=42)
179 |     >>> base_clf = GaussianNB()
180 |     >>> calibrated_clf = CalibratedClassifierCV(base_estimator=base_clf, cv=3)
181 |     >>> calibrated_clf.fit(X, y)
182 |     CalibratedClassifierCV(base_estimator=GaussianNB(), cv=3)
183 |     >>> len(calibrated_clf.calibrated_classifiers_)
184 |     3
185 |     >>> calibrated_clf.predict_proba(X)[:5, :]
186 |     array([[0.110..., 0.889...],
187 |            [0.072..., 0.927...],
188 |            [0.928..., 0.071...],
189 |            [0.928..., 0.071...],
190 |            [0.071..., 0.928...]])
191 | 
192 |     >>> from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
193 |     >>> X, y = make_classification(n_samples=100, n_features=2,
194 |     ...                            n_redundant=0, random_state=42)
195 |     >>> X_train, X_calib, y_train, y_calib = train_test_split(
196 |     ...        X, y, random_state=42
197 |     ... )
198 |     >>> base_clf = GaussianNB()
199 |     >>> base_clf.fit(X_train, y_train)
200 |     GaussianNB()
201 |     >>> calibrated_clf = CalibratedClassifierCV(
202 |     ...     base_estimator=base_clf,
203 |     ...     cv="prefit"
204 |     ... )
205 |     >>> calibrated_clf.fit(X_calib, y_calib)
206 |     CalibratedClassifierCV(base_estimator=GaussianNB(), cv='prefit')
207 |     >>> len(calibrated_clf.calibrated_classifiers_)
208 |     1
209 |     >>> calibrated_clf.predict_proba([[-0.5, 0.5]])
210 |     array([[0.936..., 0.063...]])
211 | 
212 |     References
213 |     ----------
214 |     .. [1] Obtaining calibrated probability estimates from decision trees
215 |            and naive Bayesian classifiers, B. Zadrozny & C. Elkan, ICML 2001
216 | 
217 |     .. [2] Transforming Classifier Scores into Accurate Multiclass
218 |            Probability Estimates, B. Zadrozny & C. Elkan, (KDD 2002)
219 | 
220 |     .. [3] Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines and Comparisons to
221 |            Regularized Likelihood Methods, J. Platt, (1999)
222 | 
223 |     .. [4] Predicting Good Probabilities with Supervised Learning,
224 |            A. Niculescu-Mizil & R. Caruana, ICML 2005
225 |     """
226 | 
227 |     def __init__(
228 |         self,
229 |         base_estimator=None,
230 |         *,
231 |         method="sigmoid",
232 |         cv=None,
233 |         n_jobs=None,
234 |         ensemble=True,
235 |     ):
236 |         self.base_estimator = base_estimator
237 |         self.method = method
238 |         self.cv = cv
239 |         self.n_jobs = n_jobs
240 |         self.ensemble = ensemble
241 | 
242 |     def fit(self, X, y, sample_weight=None):
243 |         """Fit the calibrated model.
244 | 
245 |         Parameters
246 |         ----------
247 |         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
248 |             Training data.
249 | 
250 |         y : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
251 |             Target values.
252 | 
253 |         sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
254 |             Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted.
255 | 
256 |         Returns
257 |         -------
258 |         self : object
259 |             Returns an instance of self.
260 |         """
261 |         check_classification_targets(y)
262 |         X, y = indexable(X, y)
263 | 
264 |         if self.base_estimator is None:
265 |             # we want all classifiers that don't expose a random_state
266 |             # to be deterministic (and we don't want to expose this one).
267 |             base_estimator = LinearSVC(random_state=0)
268 |         else:
269 |             base_estimator = self.base_estimator
270 | 
271 |         self.calibrated_classifiers_ = []
272 |         if self.cv == "prefit":
273 |             # `classes_` should be consistent with that of base_estimator
274 |             check_is_fitted(self.base_estimator, attributes=["classes_"])
275 |             self.classes_ = self.base_estimator.classes_
276 | 
277 |             pred_method, method_name = _get_prediction_method(base_estimator)
278 |             n_classes = len(self.classes_)
279 |             predictions = _compute_predictions(pred_method, method_name, X, n_classes)
280 | 
281 |             calibrated_classifier = _fit_calibrator(
282 |                 base_estimator,
283 |                 predictions,
284 |                 y,
285 |                 self.classes_,
286 |                 self.method,
287 |                 sample_weight,
288 |             )
289 |             self.calibrated_classifiers_.append(calibrated_classifier)
290 |         else:
291 |             # Set `classes_` using all `y`
292 |             label_encoder_ = LabelEncoder().fit(y)
293 |             self.classes_ = label_encoder_.classes_
294 |             n_classes = len(self.classes_)
295 | 
296 |             # sample_weight checks
297 |             fit_parameters = signature(base_estimator.fit).parameters
298 |             supports_sw = "sample_weight" in fit_parameters
299 |             if sample_weight is not None:
300 |                 sample_weight = _check_sample_weight(sample_weight, X)
301 |                 if not supports_sw:
302 |                     estimator_name = type(base_estimator).__name__
303 |                     warnings.warn(
304 |                         f"Since {estimator_name} does not support "
305 |                         "sample_weights, sample weights will only be"
306 |                         " used for the calibration itself."
307 |                     )
308 | 
309 |             # Check that each cross-validation fold can have at least one
310 |             # example per class
311 |             if isinstance(self.cv, int):
312 |                 n_folds = self.cv
313 |             elif hasattr(self.cv, "n_splits"):
314 |                 n_folds = self.cv.n_splits
315 |             else:
316 |                 n_folds = None
317 |             if n_folds and np.any(
318 |                 [np.sum(y == class_) < n_folds for class_ in self.classes_]
319 |             ):
320 |                 raise ValueError(
321 |                     f"Requesting {n_folds}-fold "
322 |                     "cross-validation but provided less than "
323 |                     f"{n_folds} examples for at least one class."
324 |                 )
325 |             cv = check_cv(self.cv, y, classifier=True)
326 | 
327 |             if self.ensemble:
328 |                 parallel = Parallel(n_jobs=self.n_jobs)
329 | 
330 |                 self.calibrated_classifiers_ = parallel(
331 |                     delayed(_fit_classifier_calibrator_pair)(
332 |                         clone(base_estimator),
333 |                         X,
334 |                         y,
335 |                         train=train,
336 |                         test=test,
337 |                         method=self.method,
338 |                         classes=self.classes_,
339 |                         supports_sw=supports_sw,
340 |                         sample_weight=sample_weight,
341 |                     )
342 |                     for train, test in cv.split(X, y)
343 |                 )
344 |             else:
345 |                 this_estimator = clone(base_estimator)
346 |                 _, method_name = _get_prediction_method(this_estimator)
347 |                 pred_method = partial(
348 |                     cross_val_predict,
349 |                     estimator=this_estimator,
350 |                     X=X,
351 |                     y=y,
352 |                     cv=cv,
353 |                     method=method_name,
354 |                     n_jobs=self.n_jobs,
355 |                 )
356 |                 predictions = _compute_predictions(
357 |                     pred_method, method_name, X, n_classes
358 |                 )
359 | 
360 |                 if sample_weight is not None and supports_sw:
361 |                     this_estimator.fit(X, y, sample_weight)
362 |                 else:
363 |                     this_estimator.fit(X, y)
364 |                 calibrated_classifier = _fit_calibrator(
365 |                     this_estimator,
366 |                     predictions,
367 |                     y,
368 |                     self.classes_,
369 |                     self.method,
370 |                     sample_weight,
371 |                 )
372 |                 self.calibrated_classifiers_.append(calibrated_classifier)
373 | 
374 |         first_clf = self.calibrated_classifiers_[0].base_estimator
375 |         if hasattr(first_clf, "n_features_in_"):
376 |             self.n_features_in_ = first_clf.n_features_in_
377 |         if hasattr(first_clf, "feature_names_in_"):
378 |             self.feature_names_in_ = first_clf.feature_names_in_
379 |         return self
380 | 
381 |     def predict_proba(self, X):
382 |         """Calibrated probabilities of classification.
383 | 
384 |         This function returns calibrated probabilities of classification
385 |         according to each class on an array of test vectors X.
386 | 
387 |         Parameters
388 |         ----------
389 |         X : The samples, as accepted by base_estimator.predict_proba
390 | 
391 |         Returns
392 |         -------
393 |         C : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_classes)
394 |             The predicted probas.
395 |         """
396 |         check_is_fitted(self)
397 |         # Compute the arithmetic mean of the predictions of the calibrated
398 |         # classifiers
399 |         mean_proba = np.zeros((_num_samples(X), len(self.classes_)))
400 |         for calibrated_classifier in self.calibrated_classifiers_:
401 |             proba = calibrated_classifier.predict_proba(X)
402 |             mean_proba += proba
403 | 
404 |         mean_proba /= len(self.calibrated_classifiers_)
405 | 
406 |         return mean_proba
407 | 
408 |     def predict(self, X):
409 |         """Predict the target of new samples. The predicted class is the
410 |         class that has the highest probability, and can thus be different
411 |         from the prediction of the uncalibrated classifier.
412 | 
413 |         Parameters
414 |         ----------
415 |         X : The samples, as accepted by base_estimator.predict
416 | 
417 |         Returns
418 |         -------
419 |         C : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
420 |             The predicted class.
421 |         """
422 |         check_is_fitted(self)
423 |         return self.classes_[np.argmax(self.predict_proba(X), axis=1)]
424 | 
425 |     def _more_tags(self):
426 |         return {
427 |             "_xfail_checks": {
428 |                 "check_sample_weights_invariance": (
429 |                     "zero sample_weight is not equivalent to removing samples"
430 |                 ),
431 |             }
432 |         }

435 | def _fit_classifier_calibrator_pair(
436 |     estimator, X, y, train, test, supports_sw, method, classes, sample_weight=None
437 | ):
438 |     """Fit a classifier/calibration pair on a given train/test split.
439 | 
440 |     Fit the classifier on the train set, compute its predictions on the test
441 |     set and use the predictions as input to fit the calibrator along with the
442 |     test labels.
443 | 
444 |     Parameters
445 |     ----------
446 |     estimator : estimator instance
447 |         Cloned base estimator.
448 | 
449 |     X : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_features)
450 |         Sample data.
451 | 
452 |     y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
453 |         Targets.
454 | 
455 |     train : ndarray, shape (n_train_indicies,)
456 |         Indices of the training subset.
457 | 
458 |     test : ndarray, shape (n_test_indicies,)
459 |         Indices of the testing subset.
460 | 
461 |     supports_sw : bool
462 |         Whether or not the `estimator` supports sample weights.
463 | 
464 |     method : {'sigmoid', 'isotonic'}
465 |         Method to use for calibration.
466 | 
467 |     classes : ndarray, shape (n_classes,)
468 |         The target classes.
469 | 
470 |     sample_weight : array-like, default=None
471 |         Sample weights for `X`.
472 | 
473 |     Returns
474 |     -------
475 |     calibrated_classifier : _CalibratedClassifier instance
476 |     """
477 |     X_train, y_train = _safe_indexing(X, train), _safe_indexing(y, train)
478 |     X_test, y_test = _safe_indexing(X, test), _safe_indexing(y, test)
479 |     if supports_sw and sample_weight is not None:
480 |         sw_train = _safe_indexing(sample_weight, train)
481 |         sw_test = _safe_indexing(sample_weight, test)
482 |     else:
483 |         sw_train = None
484 |         sw_test = None
485 | 
486 |     if supports_sw:
487 |         estimator.fit(X_train, y_train, sample_weight=sw_train)
488 |     else:
489 |         estimator.fit(X_train, y_train)
490 | 
491 |     n_classes = len(classes)
492 |     pred_method, method_name = _get_prediction_method(estimator)
493 |     predictions = _compute_predictions(pred_method, method_name, X_test, n_classes)
494 | 
495 |     calibrated_classifier = _fit_calibrator(
496 |         estimator, predictions, y_test, classes, method, sample_weight=sw_test
497 |     )
498 |     return calibrated_classifier
499 | 
500 | 
501 | def _get_prediction_method(clf):
502 |     """Return prediction method.
503 | 
504 |     `decision_function` method of `clf` returned, if it
505 |     exists, otherwise `predict_proba` method returned.
506 | 
507 |     Parameters
508 |     ----------
509 |     clf : Estimator instance
510 |         Fitted classifier to obtain the prediction method from.
511 | 
512 |     Returns
513 |     -------
514 |     prediction_method : callable
515 |         The prediction method.
516 |     method_name : str
517 |         The name of the prediction method.
518 |     """
519 |     if hasattr(clf, "decision_function"):
520 |         method = getattr(clf, "decision_function")
521 |         return method, "decision_function"
522 |     elif hasattr(clf, "predict_proba"):
523 |         method = getattr(clf, "predict_proba")
524 |         return method, "predict_proba"
525 |     else:
526 |         raise RuntimeError(
527 |             "'base_estimator' has no 'decision_function' or 'predict_proba' method."
528 |         )
529 | 
530 | 
531 | def _compute_predictions(pred_method, method_name, X, n_classes):
532 |     """Return predictions for `X` and reshape binary outputs to shape
533 |     (n_samples, 1).
534 | 
535 |     Parameters
536 |     ----------
537 |     pred_method : callable
538 |         Prediction method.
539 | 
540 |     method_name: str
541 |         Name of the prediction method
542 | 
543 |     X : array-like or None
544 |         Data used to obtain predictions.
545 | 
546 |     n_classes : int
547 |         Number of classes present.
548 | 
549 |     Returns
550 |     -------
551 |     predictions : array-like, shape (X.shape[0], len(clf.classes_))
552 |         The predictions. Note if there are 2 classes, array is of shape
553 |         (X.shape[0], 1).
554 |     """
555 |     predictions = pred_method(X=X)
556 | 
557 |     if method_name == "decision_function":
558 |         if predictions.ndim == 1:
559 |             predictions = predictions[:, np.newaxis]
560 |     elif method_name == "predict_proba":
561 |         if n_classes == 2:
562 |             predictions = predictions[:, 1:]
563 |     else:  # pragma: no cover
564 |         # this branch should be unreachable.
565 |         raise ValueError(f"Invalid prediction method: {method_name}")
566 |     return predictions
567 | 
568 | 
569 | def _fit_calibrator(clf, predictions, y, classes, method, sample_weight=None):
570 |     """Fit calibrator(s) and return a `_CalibratedClassifier`
571 |     instance.
572 | 
573 |     `n_classes` (i.e. `len(clf.classes_)`) calibrators are fitted.
574 |     However, if `n_classes` equals 2, one calibrator is fitted.
575 | 
576 |     Parameters
577 |     ----------
578 |     clf : estimator instance
579 |         Fitted classifier.
580 | 
581 |     predictions : array-like, shape (n_samples, n_classes) or (n_samples, 1) \
582 |                     when binary.
583 |         Raw predictions returned by the un-calibrated base classifier.
584 | 
585 |     y : array-like, shape (n_samples,)
586 |         The targets.
587 | 
588 |     classes : ndarray, shape (n_classes,)
589 |         All the prediction classes.
590 | 
591 |     method : {'sigmoid', 'isotonic'}
592 |         The method to use for calibration.
593 | 
594 |     sample_weight : ndarray, shape (n_samples,), default=None
595 |         Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted.
596 | 
597 |     Returns
598 |     -------
599 |     pipeline : _CalibratedClassifier instance
600 |     """
601 |     Y = label_binarize(y, classes=classes)
602 |     label_encoder = LabelEncoder().fit(classes)
603 |     pos_class_indices = label_encoder.transform(clf.classes_)
604 |     calibrators = []
605 |     for class_idx, this_pred in zip(pos_class_indices, predictions.T):
606 |         if method == "isotonic":
607 |             calibrator = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds="clip")
608 |         elif method == "sigmoid":
609 |             calibrator = _SigmoidCalibration()
610 |         else:
611 |             raise ValueError(
612 |                 f"'method' should be one of: 'sigmoid' or 'isotonic'. Got {method}."
613 |             )
614 |         calibrator.fit(this_pred, Y[:, class_idx], sample_weight)
615 |         calibrators.append(calibrator)
616 | 
617 |     pipeline = _CalibratedClassifier(clf, calibrators, method=method, classes=classes)
618 |     return pipeline

621 | class _CalibratedClassifier:
622 |     """Pipeline-like chaining a fitted classifier and its fitted calibrators.
623 | 
624 |     Parameters
625 |     ----------
626 |     base_estimator : estimator instance
627 |         Fitted classifier.
628 | 
629 |     calibrators : list of fitted estimator instances
630 |         List of fitted calibrators (either 'IsotonicRegression' or
631 |         '_SigmoidCalibration'). The number of calibrators equals the number of
632 |         classes. However, if there are 2 classes, the list contains only one
633 |         fitted calibrator.
634 | 
635 |     classes : array-like of shape (n_classes,)
636 |         All the prediction classes.
637 | 
638 |     method : {'sigmoid', 'isotonic'}, default='sigmoid'
639 |         The method to use for calibration. Can be 'sigmoid' which
640 |         corresponds to Platt's method or 'isotonic' which is a
641 |         non-parametric approach based on isotonic regression.
642 | 
643 |     Attributes
644 |     ----------
645 |     calibrators_ : list of fitted estimator instances
646 |         Same as `calibrators`. Exposed for backward-compatibility. Use
647 |         `calibrators` instead.
648 | 
649 |         .. deprecated:: 0.24
650 |            `calibrators_` is deprecated from 0.24 and will be removed in
651 |            1.1 (renaming of 0.26). Use `calibrators` instead.
652 |     """
653 | 
654 |     def __init__(self, base_estimator, calibrators, *, classes, method="sigmoid"):
655 |         self.base_estimator = base_estimator
656 |         self.calibrators = calibrators
657 |         self.classes = classes
658 |         self.method = method
659 | 
660 |     # TODO: Remove in 1.1
661 |     # mypy error: Decorated property not supported
662 |     @deprecated(  # type: ignore
663 |         "`calibrators_` is deprecated in 0.24 and will be removed in 1.1"
664 |         "(renaming of 0.26). Use `calibrators` instead."
665 |     )
666 |     @property
667 |     def calibrators_(self):
668 |         return self.calibrators
669 | 
670 |     def predict_proba(self, X):
671 |         """Calculate calibrated probabilities.
672 | 
673 |         Calculates classification calibrated probabilities
674 |         for each class, in a one-vs-all manner, for `X`.
675 | 
676 |         Parameters
677 |         ----------
678 |         X : ndarray of shape (n_samples, n_features)
679 |             The sample data.
680 | 
681 |         Returns
682 |         -------
683 |         proba : array, shape (n_samples, n_classes)
684 |             The predicted probabilities. Can be exact zeros.
685 |         """
686 |         n_classes = len(self.classes)
687 |         pred_method, method_name = _get_prediction_method(self.base_estimator)
688 |         predictions = _compute_predictions(pred_method, method_name, X, n_classes)
689 | 
690 |         label_encoder = LabelEncoder().fit(self.classes)
691 |         pos_class_indices = label_encoder.transform(self.base_estimator.classes_)
692 | 
693 |         proba = np.zeros((_num_samples(X), n_classes))
694 |         for class_idx, this_pred, calibrator in zip(
695 |             pos_class_indices, predictions.T, self.calibrators
696 |         ):
697 |             if n_classes == 2:
698 |                 # When binary, `predictions` consists only of predictions for
699 |                 # clf.classes_[1] but `pos_class_indices` = 0
700 |                 class_idx += 1
701 |             proba[:, class_idx] = calibrator.predict(this_pred)
702 | 
703 |         # Normalize the probabilities
704 |         if n_classes == 2:
705 |             proba[:, 0] = 1.0 - proba[:, 1]
706 |         else:
707 |             denominator = np.sum(proba, axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]
708 |             # In the edge case where for each class calibrator returns a null
709 |             # probability for a given sample, use the uniform distribution
710 |             # instead.
711 |             uniform_proba = np.full_like(proba, 1 / n_classes)
712 |             proba = np.divide(
713 |                 proba, denominator, out=uniform_proba, where=denominator != 0
714 |             )
715 | 
716 |         # Deal with cases where the predicted probability minimally exceeds 1.0
717 |         proba[(1.0 < proba) & (proba <= 1.0 + 1e-5)] = 1.0
718 | 
719 |         return proba
720 | 
721 | 
722 | def _sigmoid_calibration(predictions, y, sample_weight=None):
723 |     """Probability Calibration with sigmoid method (Platt 2000)
724 | 
725 |     Parameters
726 |     ----------
727 |     predictions : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
728 |         The decision function or predict proba for the samples.
729 | 
730 |     y : ndarray of shape (n_samples,)
731 |         The targets.
732 | 
733 |     sample_weight : array-like of shape (n_samples,), default=None
734 |         Sample weights. If None, then samples are equally weighted.
735 | 
736 |     Returns
737 |     -------
738 |     a : float
739 |         The slope.
740 | 
741 |     b : float
742 |         The intercept.
743 | 
744 |     References
745 |     ----------
746 |     Platt, "Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines"
747 |     """
748 |     predictions = column_or_1d(predictions)
749 |     y = column_or_1d(y)
750 | 
751 |     F = predictions  # F follows Platt's notations
752 | 
753 |     # Bayesian priors (see Platt end of section 2.2)
754 |     prior0 = float(np.sum(y <= 0))
755 |     prior1 = y.shape[0] - prior0
756 |     T = np.zeros(y.shape)
757 |     T[y > 0] = (prior1 + 1.0) / (prior1 + 2.0)
758 |     T[y <= 0] = 1.0 / (prior0 + 2.0)
759 |     T1 = 1.0 - T
760 | 
761 |     def objective(AB):
762 |         # From Platt (beginning of Section 2.2)

Searches the codebase to retrieve relevant code snippets based on given queries(terms or line numbers).
** Note:
- Either `search_terms` or `line_nums` must be provided to perform a search.
- If `search_terms` are provided, it searches for code snippets based on each term:
- If `line_nums` is provided, it searches for code snippets around the specified lines within the file defined by `file_path_or_pattern`.

** Example Usage:
# Search for code content contain keyword `order`, `bill`
search_code_snippets(search_terms=["order", "bill"])

# Search for a class
search_code_snippets(search_terms=["MyClass"])

# Search for context around specific lines (10 and 15) within a file

search_terms.description: A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase. This can include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments. Either `search_terms` or `line_nums` must be provided to perform a search.

line_nums.description: Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file. Must be used alongside a valid `file_path_or_pattern`. Either `line_nums` or `search_terms` must be provided to perform a search.

file_path_or_pattern.description: A glob pattern or specific file path used to filter search results to particular files or directories. Defaults to "**/*.py", meaning all Python files are searched by default. If `line_nums` are provided, this must specify a specific file path.

The tool can handle specific entity queries such as function names, class names, or file paths.

**Usage Example:**

For functions or classes, the format should be 'file_path:QualifiedName' (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum'). For files, use just the file path (e.g., 'src/my_file.py').

function.name: explore_tree_structure
function.description:
Unified repository exploring tool that traverses a pre-built code graph to retrieve dependency structure around specified entities.
The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.

Code Graph Definition:
* Entity Types: 'directory', 'file', 'class', 'function'.
* Dependency Types: 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits'.
* Hierarchy:
    - Directories contain files and subdirectories.
    - Files contain classes and functions.
    - Classes contain inner classes and methods.
    - Functions can contain inner functions.
* Interactions:
    - Files/classes/functions can import classes and functions.
    - Classes can inherit from other classes.
    - Classes and functions can invoke others (invocations in a class's `__init__` are attributed to the class).
Entity ID:
* Unique identifier including file path and module path.
* Here's an example of an Entity ID: `"interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func"` identifies function `inner_func` within `method_a` of class `C` in `"interface/C.py"`.

Notes:
* Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
* Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.


Example Usage:
1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
        direction='downstream',
        traversal_depth=2,
        dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.

2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
        direction='upstream',
        traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
3. Exploring Repository Structure:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
      start_entities=['/'],
      traversal_depth=2,
      dependency_type_filter=['contains']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the tree repository structure from the root directory (/), traversing up to two levels deep and focusing only on 'contains' relationship.
4. Generate Class Diagrams:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=selected_entity_ids,
        direction='both',
        traverse_depth=-1,
        dependency_type_filter=['inherits']
    )
    ```

start_entities.description:
List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName" (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).

direction.description:
Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are: `upstream`, `downstream`, `both`.
- 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
- 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others (how others depend on them).
- 'both': Traversal on both direction.

traversal_depth.description: Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).

entity_type_filter.description: List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal. If None, all entity types are included.

dependency_type_filter.description: List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal. If None, all dependency types are included.

search_terms.description: A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase. This can include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments. Either `search_terms` or `line_nums` must be provided to perform a search.

line_nums.description: Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file. Must be used alongside a valid `file_path_or_pattern`. Either `line_nums` or `search_terms` must be provided to perform a search.

file_path_or_pattern.description: A glob pattern or specific file path used to filter search results to particular files or directories. Defaults to "**/*.py", meaning all Python files are searched by default. If `line_nums` are provided, this must specify a specific file path.

function.name: get_entity_contents

Searches the codebase to retrieve the complete implementations of specified entities based on the provided entity names. 
The tool can handle specific entity queries such as function names, class names, or file paths.

entity_names.description: A list of entity names to query. Each entity name can represent a function, class, or file. For functions or classes, the format should be 'file_path:QualifiedName' (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum'). For files, use just the file path (e.g., 'src/my_file.py').

function.name: explore_tree_structure
function.description:
Unified repository exploring tool that traverses a pre-built code graph to retrieve dependency structure around specified entities.
The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.

Code Graph Definition:
* Entity Types: 'directory', 'file', 'class', 'function'.
* Dependency Types: 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits'.
* Hierarchy:
    - Directories contain files and subdirectories.
    - Files contain classes and functions.
    - Classes contain inner classes and methods.
    - Functions can contain inner functions.
* Interactions:
    - Files/classes/functions can import classes and functions.
    - Classes can inherit from other classes.
    - Classes and functions can invoke others (invocations in a class's `__init__` are attributed to the class).
Entity ID:
* Unique identifier including file path and module path.
* Here's an example of an Entity ID: `"interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func"` identifies function `inner_func` within `method_a` of class `C` in `"interface/C.py"`.

Notes:
* Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
* Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.


Example Usage:
1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
        direction='downstream',
        traversal_depth=2,
        dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.

2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
        direction='upstream',
        traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
3. Exploring Repository Structure:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
      start_entities=['/'],
      traversal_depth=2,
      dependency_type_filter=['contains']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the tree repository structure from the root directory (/), traversing up to two levels deep and focusing only on 'contains' relationship.
4. Generate Class Diagrams:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=selected_entity_ids,
        direction='both',
        traverse_depth=-1,
        dependency_type_filter=['inherits']
    )
    ```

start_entities.description:
List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName" (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).

direction.description:
Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are: `upstream`, `downstream`, `both`.
- 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
- 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others (how others depend on them).
- 'both': Traversal on both direction.

traversal_depth.description: Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).

entity_type_filter.description: List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal. If None, all entity types are included.

dependency_type_filter.description: List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal. If None, all dependency types are included.

meta_data.problem_statement:
MAINT conversion old->new/new->old tags
Towards #30298 

This PR provides a way to convert old tags into new tags and new tags into old tags.
We should make sure that:

- An estimator implementing `_get_tags` or `_more_tags` get a warning but that the check_estimator should be working reasonably
- `_safe_tags` should raise a deprecation warning
- we should make sure that `get_tags` can get old tags and convert it to new tags. The tricky part is to detect whether `__sklearn_tags__` if present is implemented by the `BaseEstimator` from scikit-learn or the child class. If this is only the `BaseEstimator`, we should raise a warning to move to the new API and we should temporary use the `_get_tags`/`_safe_tags`, otherwise we are fine.

    - If a term matches a file, class, or function name, matched entities are retrieved.
    - If there is no match with any module name, it attempts to find code snippets that likely contain the term.
    2. If `line_nums` is provided, it searches for code snippets at the specified lines within the file defined by
    `file_path_or_pattern`.
    Args:
    search_terms (Optional[List[str]]): A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase.
    Terms can be formatted as 'file_path:QualifiedName' to search for a specific module or entity within a file
    (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum') or as 'file_path' to retrieve the complete content
    of a file. This can also include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments.
    line_nums (Optional[List[int]]): Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file.
    When provided, `file_path_or_pattern` must specify a valid file path.

function.name: explore_tree_structure
function.description:
Unified repository exploring tool that traverses a pre-built code graph to retrieve dependency structure around specified entities.
The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.

Code Graph Definition:
* Entity Types: 'directory', 'file', 'class', 'function'.
* Dependency Types: 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits'.
* Hierarchy:
    - Directories contain files and subdirectories.
    - Files contain classes and functions.
    - Classes contain inner classes and methods.
    - Functions can contain inner functions.
* Interactions:
    - Files/classes/functions can import classes and functions.
    - Classes can inherit from other classes.
    - Classes and functions can invoke others (invocations in a class's `__init__` are attributed to the class).
Entity ID:
* Unique identifier including file path and module path.
* Here's an example of an Entity ID: `"interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func"` identifies function `inner_func` within `method_a` of class `C` in `"interface/C.py"`.

Notes:
* Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
* Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.


Example Usage:
1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
        direction='downstream',
        traversal_depth=2,
        dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.

2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
        direction='upstream',
        traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
3. Exploring Repository Structure:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
      start_entities=['/'],
      traversal_depth=2,
      dependency_type_filter=['contains']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the tree repository structure from the root directory (/), traversing up to two levels deep and focusing only on 'contains' relationship.
4. Generate Class Diagrams:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=selected_entity_ids,
        direction='both',
        traverse_depth=-1,
        dependency_type_filter=['inherits']
    )
    ```

start_entities.description:
List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName" (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).

direction.description:
Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are: `upstream`, `downstream`, `both`.
- 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
- 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others (how others depend on them).
- 'both': Traversal on both direction.

traversal_depth.description: Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).

entity_type_filter.description: List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal. If None, all entity types are included.

dependency_type_filter.description: List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal. If None, all dependency types are included.

meta_data.problem_statement:
Reduce redundancy in floating type checks for Array API support
### Describe the workflow you want to enable

While working on #29978, we noticed that the following procedure is repeated across most regression metrics in `_regression.py` for the Array API:

```python
    xp, _ = get_namespace(y_true, y_pred, sample_weight, multioutput)
    dtype = _find_matching_floating_dtype(y_true, y_pred, xp=xp)

    _, y_true, y_pred, multioutput = _check_reg_targets(
        y_true, y_pred, multioutput, dtype=dtype, xp=xp
    )
```

To reduce redundancy, it would make sense to incorporate the `_find_matching_floating_dtype` logic directly into the `_check_reg_targets` function. This would result in the following cleaner implementation:

```python
    xp, _ = get_namespace(y_true, y_pred, sample_weight, multioutput)
    _, y_true, y_pred, multioutput, dtype = _check_reg_targets(

A chat between a curious user and an artificial intelligence assistant. The assistant gives helpful, detailed answers to the user's questions.

search_code_snippets(search_terms: Optional[List[str]] = None, line_nums: Optional[List] = None, file_path_or_pattern: Optional[str] = '**/*.py') -> str:
    Searches the codebase to retrieve relevant code snippets based on given queries(terms or line numbers).
    This function supports retrieving the complete content of a code entity,
    searching for code entities such as classes or functions by keywords, or locating specific lines within a file.
    It also supports filtering searches based on a file path or file pattern.
    Note:
    1. If `search_terms` are provided, it searches for code snippets based on each term:
    - If a term is formatted as 'file_path:QualifiedName' (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum') ,
    or just 'file_path', the corresponding complete code is retrieved or file content is retrieved.
    - If a term matches a file, class, or function name, matched entities are retrieved.
    - If there is no match with any module name, it attempts to find code snippets that likely contain the term.
    2. If `line_nums` is provided, it searches for code snippets at the specified lines within the file defined by
    `file_path_or_pattern`.
    Args:
    search_terms (Optional[List[str]]): A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase.
    Terms can be formatted as 'file_path:QualifiedName' to search for a specific module or entity within a file
    (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum') or as 'file_path' to retrieve the complete content
    of a file. This can also include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments.
    line_nums (Optional[List[int]]): Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file.
    When provided, `file_path_or_pattern` must specify a valid file path.
    file_path_or_pattern (Optional[str]): A glob pattern or specific file path used to filter search results
    to particular files or directories. Defaults to '**/*.py', meaning all Python files are searched by default.
    If `line_nums` are provided, this must specify a specific file path.
    Returns:
    str: The search results, which may include code snippets, matching entities, or complete file content.
    Example Usage:
    # Search for the full content of a specific file
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=['src/my_file.py'])
    # Search for a specific function
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=['src/my_file.py:MyClass.func_name'])
    # Search for specific lines (10 and 15) within a file
    result = search_code_snippets(line_nums=[10, 15], file_path_or_pattern='src/example.py')
    # Combined search for a module name and within a specific file pattern
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=["MyClass"], file_path_or_pattern="src/**/*.py")

explore_graph_structure(start_entities: List[str], direction: str = 'downstream', traversal_depth: int = 1, entity_type_filter: Optional[List[str]] = None, dependency_type_filter: Optional[List[str]] = None):

    Analyzes and displays the dependency structure around specified entities in a code graph.
    This function searches and presents relationships and dependencies for the specified entities (such as classes, functions, files, or directories) in a code graph.
    It explores how the input entities relate to others, using defined types of dependencies, including 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes' and 'inherits'.
    The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.
    Example Usage:
    1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    get_local_structure(
    start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
    direction='downstream',
    traversal_depth=2,
    entity_type_filter=['class', 'function'],
    dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.
    2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    get_local_structure(
    start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
    direction='upstream',
    traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
    Notes:
    * Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
    * Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.
    * Graph Context: The function operates on a pre-built code graph containing entities (e.g., files, classes and functions) and dependencies representing their interactions and relationships.
    Parameters:
    ----------
    start_entities : list[str]
    List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
    - Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName"
    (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
    - For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).
    direction : str, optional
    Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are:
    - 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
    - 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others
    (how others depend on them).
    - 'both': Traversal in both directions.
    Default is 'downstream'.
    traversal_depth : int, optional
    Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).
    Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).
    Default is 2.
    entity_type_filter : list[str], optional
    List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal.
    If None, all entity types are included.
    Default is None.
    dependency_type_filter : list[str], optional
    List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal.
    If None, all dependency types are included.
    Default is None.
    Returns:
    -------
    result : object
    An object representing the traversal results, which includes discovered entities and their dependencies.

674 |     """Find a suitable floating point dtype when computing with arrays.

687 |     ]
688 |     if floating_dtypes:
689 |         # Return the floating dtype with the highest precision:

function.name: search_code_snippets
function.description:
Searches the codebase to retrieve relevant code snippets based on given queries(terms or line numbers).
** Note:
- Either `search_terms` or `line_nums` must be provided to perform a search.
- If `search_terms` are provided, it searches for code snippets based on each term:
- If `line_nums` is provided, it searches for code snippets around the specified lines within the file defined by `file_path_or_pattern`.

** Example Usage:
# Search for code content contain keyword `order`, `bill`
search_code_snippets(search_terms=["order", "bill"])

# Search for a class
search_code_snippets(search_terms=["MyClass"])

# Search for context around specific lines (10 and 15) within a file
search_code_snippets(line_nums=[10, 15], file_path_or_pattern='src/example.py')

search_terms.description: A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase. This can include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments. Either `search_terms` or `line_nums` must be provided to perform a search.

line_nums.description: Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file. Must be used alongside a valid `file_path_or_pattern`. Either `line_nums` or `search_terms` must be provided to perform a search.

file_path_or_pattern.description: A glob pattern or specific file path used to filter search results to particular files or directories. Defaults to "**/*.py", meaning all Python files are searched by default. If `line_nums` are provided, this must specify a specific file path.

function.name: get_entity_contents

The tool can handle specific entity queries such as function names, class names, or file paths.

For functions or classes, the format should be 'file_path:QualifiedName' (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum'). For files, use just the file path (e.g., 'src/my_file.py').

function.name: explore_tree_structure
function.description:
Unified repository exploring tool that traverses a pre-built code graph to retrieve dependency structure around specified entities.
The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.

Code Graph Definition:
* Entity Types: 'directory', 'file', 'class', 'function'.
* Dependency Types: 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits'.
* Hierarchy:
    - Directories contain files and subdirectories.
    - Files contain classes and functions.
    - Classes contain inner classes and methods.
    - Functions can contain inner functions.
* Interactions:
    - Files/classes/functions can import classes and functions.
    - Classes can inherit from other classes.
    - Classes and functions can invoke others (invocations in a class's `__init__` are attributed to the class).
Entity ID:
* Unique identifier including file path and module path.
* Here's an example of an Entity ID: `"interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func"` identifies function `inner_func` within `method_a` of class `C` in `"interface/C.py"`.

Notes:
* Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
* Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.


Example Usage:
1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
        direction='downstream',
        traversal_depth=2,
        dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.

2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
        direction='upstream',
        traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
3. Exploring Repository Structure:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
      start_entities=['/'],
      traversal_depth=2,
      dependency_type_filter=['contains']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the tree repository structure from the root directory (/), traversing up to two levels deep and focusing only on 'contains' relationship.
4. Generate Class Diagrams:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=selected_entity_ids,
        direction='both',
        traverse_depth=-1,
        dependency_type_filter=['inherits']
    )
    ```

start_entities.description:
List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName" (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).

direction.description:
Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are: `upstream`, `downstream`, `both`.
- 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
- 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others (how others depend on them).
- 'both': Traversal on both direction.

traversal_depth.description: Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).

entity_type_filter.description: List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal. If None, all entity types are included.

dependency_type_filter.description: List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal. If None, all dependency types are included.

This tool reads `DaLIC/vt_results/<instance_id>/unique_artifacts.json` and returns a short JSON summary.
It does not rank or recommend results. It only applies exact filters and pagination.

Usage suggestions:
- Call this once near the start of analyzing a new data point to inspect execution-trace evidence.
- Call it again later with narrower `path_contains` or `name_contains` filters whenever you need a more precise slice.

artifact_type.description: Optional exact filter for artifact definition type.

path_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the compact file path.

name_contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the qualified name.

limit.description: Maximum number of artifacts to return in this slice.

Based on the analysis of the issue and the code, I can now provide the locations that need modification. The issue is about improving error messages when using the `.str` accessor with incorrect data types.

Here are the relevant locations:

```
pandas/core/strings/accessor.py
line: 257-259
function: StringMethods._validate

pandas/core/arrays/arrow/accessors.py
line: 47-55
function: ArrowAccessor._validate

pandas/core/accessor.py
line: 201-204
class: Accessor
```

The main issue is in the error handling of string accessor validation. Currently, when an invalid dtype is used with the `.str` accessor, it raises an AttributeError with a generic message:

```python
raise AttributeError("Can only use .str accessor with string values!")
```

Instead, it should include the inferred dtype that caused the error. This is happening in multiple places:

1. The primary validation in `StringMethods._validate()` which is called when trying to access `.str` functionality on a Series or Index

2. The Arrow accessor validation logic in `ArrowAccessor._validate()` which performs similar error checking

3. The base accessor class validation in `pandas/core/accessor.py` which could be extended to include more general error message improvements

These locations are listed in order of importance for implementing the improved error messages. The main change would likely be in the `_validate` method of `StringMethods` since it's the most commonly used accessor and the error message improvement would benefit most users.

By replacing:

search_code_snippets(search_terms: Optional[List[str]] = None, line_nums: Optional[List] = None, file_path_or_pattern: Optional[str] = '**/*.py') -> str:
    Searches the codebase to retrieve relevant code snippets based on given queries(terms or line numbers).
    This function supports retrieving the complete content of a code entity,
    searching for code entities such as classes or functions by keywords, or locating specific lines within a file.
    It also supports filtering searches based on a file path or file pattern.
    Note:
    1. If `search_terms` are provided, it searches for code snippets based on each term:
    - If a term is formatted as 'file_path:QualifiedName' (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum') ,
    or just 'file_path', the corresponding complete code is retrieved or file content is retrieved.
    - If a term matches a file, class, or function name, matched entities are retrieved.
    - If there is no match with any module name, it attempts to find code snippets that likely contain the term.
    2. If `line_nums` is provided, it searches for code snippets at the specified lines within the file defined by
    `file_path_or_pattern`.
    Args:
    search_terms (Optional[List[str]]): A list of names, keywords, or code snippets to search for within the codebase.
    Terms can be formatted as 'file_path:QualifiedName' to search for a specific module or entity within a file
    (e.g., 'src/helpers/math_helpers.py:MathUtils.calculate_sum') or as 'file_path' to retrieve the complete content
    of a file. This can also include potential function names, class names, or general code fragments.
    line_nums (Optional[List[int]]): Specific line numbers to locate code snippets within a specified file.
    When provided, `file_path_or_pattern` must specify a valid file path.
    file_path_or_pattern (Optional[str]): A glob pattern or specific file path used to filter search results
    to particular files or directories. Defaults to '**/*.py', meaning all Python files are searched by default.
    If `line_nums` are provided, this must specify a specific file path.
    Returns:
    str: The search results, which may include code snippets, matching entities, or complete file content.
    Example Usage:
    # Search for the full content of a specific file
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=['src/my_file.py'])
    # Search for a specific function
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=['src/my_file.py:MyClass.func_name'])
    # Search for specific lines (10 and 15) within a file
    result = search_code_snippets(line_nums=[10, 15], file_path_or_pattern='src/example.py')
    # Combined search for a module name and within a specific file pattern
    result = search_code_snippets(search_terms=["MyClass"], file_path_or_pattern="src/**/*.py")

    Analyzes and displays the dependency structure around specified entities in a code graph.
    This function searches and presents relationships and dependencies for the specified entities (such as classes, functions, files, or directories) in a code graph.
    It explores how the input entities relate to others, using defined types of dependencies, including 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes' and 'inherits'.
    The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.
    Example Usage:
    1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    get_local_structure(
    start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
    direction='downstream',
    traversal_depth=2,
    entity_type_filter=['class', 'function'],
    dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.
    2. Exploring Inward Dependencies:
    ```
    get_local_structure(
    start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
    direction='upstream',
    traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
    Notes:
    * Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
    * Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.
    * Graph Context: The function operates on a pre-built code graph containing entities (e.g., files, classes and functions) and dependencies representing their interactions and relationships.
    Parameters:
    ----------
    start_entities : list[str]
    List of entities (e.g., class, function, file, or directory paths) to begin the search from.
    - Entities representing classes or functions must be formatted as "file_path:QualifiedName"
    (e.g., `interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func`).
    - For files or directories, provide only the file or directory path (e.g., `src/module_a.py` or `src/`).
    direction : str, optional
    Direction of traversal in the code graph; allowed options are:
    - 'upstream': Traversal to explore dependencies that the specified entities rely on (how they depend on others).
    - 'downstream': Traversal to explore the effects or interactions of the specified entities on others
    (how others depend on them).
    - 'both': Traversal in both directions.
    Default is 'downstream'.
    traversal_depth : int, optional
    Maximum depth of traversal. A value of -1 indicates unlimited depth (subject to a maximum limit).
    Must be either `-1` or a non-negative integer (≥ 0).
    Default is 2.
    entity_type_filter : list[str], optional
    List of entity types (e.g., 'class', 'function', 'file', 'directory') to include in the traversal.
    If None, all entity types are included.
    Default is None.
    dependency_type_filter : list[str], optional
    List of dependency types (e.g., 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits') to include in the traversal.
    If None, all dependency types are included.
    Default is None.
    Returns:
    -------
    result : object
    An object representing the traversal results, which includes discovered entities and their dependencies.

Description: 
Unified repository exploring tool that traverses a pre-built code graph to retrieve dependency structure around specified entities.
The search can be controlled to traverse upstream (exploring dependencies that entities rely on) or downstream (exploring how entities impact others), with optional limits on traversal depth and filters for entity and dependency types.

Code Graph Definition:
* Entity Types: 'directory', 'file', 'class', 'function'.
* Dependency Types: 'contains', 'imports', 'invokes', 'inherits'.
* Hierarchy:
    - Directories contain files and subdirectories.
    - Files contain classes and functions.
    - Classes contain inner classes and methods.
    - Functions can contain inner functions.
* Interactions:
    - Files/classes/functions can import classes and functions.
    - Classes can inherit from other classes.
    - Classes and functions can invoke others (invocations in a class's `__init__` are attributed to the class).
Entity ID:
* Unique identifier including file path and module path.
* Here's an example of an Entity ID: `"interface/C.py:C.method_a.inner_func"` identifies function `inner_func` within `method_a` of class `C` in `"interface/C.py"`.

Notes:
* Traversal Control: The `traversal_depth` parameter specifies how deep the function should explore the graph starting from the input entities.
* Filtering: Use `entity_type_filter` and `dependency_type_filter` to narrow down the scope of the search, focusing on specific entity types and relationships.


Example Usage:
1. Exploring Outward Dependencies:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_a.py:ClassA'],
        direction='downstream',
        traversal_depth=2,
        dependency_type_filter=['invokes', 'imports']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the dependencies of `ClassA` up to 2 levels deep, focusing only on classes and functions with 'invokes' and 'imports' relationships.

    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=['src/module_b.py:FunctionY'],
        direction='upstream',
        traversal_depth=-1
    )
    ```
    This finds all entities that depend on `FunctionY` without restricting the traversal depth.
3. Exploring Repository Structure:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
      start_entities=['/'],
      traversal_depth=2,
      dependency_type_filter=['contains']
    )
    ```
    This retrieves the tree repository structure from the root directory (/), traversing up to two levels deep and focusing only on 'contains' relationship.
4. Generate Class Diagrams:
    ```
    explore_tree_structure(
        start_entities=selected_entity_ids,
        direction='both',
        traverse_depth=-1,
        dependency_type_filter=['inherits']
    )
    ```

  79 | def forbid_nonstring_types(
  80 |     forbidden: list[str] | None, name: str | None = None
  81 | ) -> Callable[[F], F]:
  82 |     """
  83 |     Decorator to forbid specific types for a method of StringMethods.
  84 | 
  85 |     For calling `.str.{method}` on a Series or Index, it is necessary to first
  86 |     initialize the :class:`StringMethods` object, and then call the method.
  87 |     However, different methods allow different input types, and so this can not
  88 |     be checked during :meth:`StringMethods.__init__`, but must be done on a
  89 |     per-method basis. This decorator exists to facilitate this process, and
  90 |     make it explicit which (inferred) types are disallowed by the method.
  91 | 
  92 |     :meth:`StringMethods.__init__` allows the *union* of types its different
  93 |     methods allow (after skipping NaNs; see :meth:`StringMethods._validate`),
  94 |     namely: ['string', 'empty', 'bytes', 'mixed', 'mixed-integer'].
  95 | 
  96 |     The default string types ['string', 'empty'] are allowed for all methods.
  97 |     For the additional types ['bytes', 'mixed', 'mixed-integer'], each method
  98 |     then needs to forbid the types it is not intended for.
  99 | 
 100 |     Parameters
 101 |     ----------
 102 |     forbidden : list-of-str or None
 103 |         List of forbidden non-string types, may be one or more of
 104 |         `['bytes', 'mixed', 'mixed-integer']`.
 105 |     name : str, default None
 106 |         Name of the method to use in the error message. By default, this is
 107 |         None, in which case the name from the method being wrapped will be
 108 |         copied. However, for working with further wrappers (like _pat_wrapper
 109 |         and _noarg_wrapper), it is necessary to specify the name.
 110 | 
 111 |     Returns
 112 |     -------
 113 |     func : wrapper
 114 |         The method to which the decorator is applied, with an added check that
 115 |         enforces the inferred type to not be in the list of forbidden types.
 116 | 
 117 |     Raises
 118 |     ------
 119 |     TypeError
 120 |         If the inferred type of the underlying data is in `forbidden`.
 121 |     """
 122 |     # deal with None
 123 |     forbidden = [] if forbidden is None else forbidden
 124 | 
 125 |     allowed_types = {"string", "empty", "bytes", "mixed", "mixed-integer"} - set(
 126 |         forbidden
 127 |     )
 128 | 
 129 |     def _forbid_nonstring_types(func: F) -> F:
 130 |         func_name = func.__name__ if name is None else name
 131 | 
 132 |         @wraps(func)
 133 |         def wrapper(self, *args, **kwargs):
 134 |             if self._inferred_dtype not in allowed_types:
 135 |                 msg = (
 136 |                     f"Cannot use .str.{func_name} with values of "
 137 |                     f"inferred dtype '{self._inferred_dtype}'."
 138 |                 )
 139 |                 raise TypeError(msg)
 140 |             return func(self, *args, **kwargs)
 141 | 
 142 |         wrapper.__name__ = func_name
 143 |         return cast(F, wrapper)
 144 | 
 145 |     return _forbid_nonstring_types
 146 | 
 147 | 
 148 | def _map_and_wrap(name: str | None, docstring: str | None):
 149 |     @forbid_nonstring_types(["bytes"], name=name)
 150 |     def wrapper(self):
 151 |         result = getattr(self._data.array, f"_str_{name}")()
 152 |         return self._wrap_result(
 153 |             result, returns_string=name not in ("isnumeric", "isdecimal")
 154 |         )
 155 | 
 156 |     wrapper.__doc__ = docstring
 157 |     return wrapper

 424 |     def _get_series_list(self, others):
 425 |         """
 426 |         Auxiliary function for :meth:`str.cat`. Turn potentially mixed input
 427 |         into a list of Series (elements without an index must match the length
 428 |         of the calling Series/Index).
 429 | 
 430 |         Parameters
 431 |         ----------
 432 |         others : Series, DataFrame, np.ndarray, list-like or list-like of
 433 |             Objects that are either Series, Index or np.ndarray (1-dim).
 434 | 
 435 |         Returns
 436 |         -------
 437 |         list of Series
 438 |             Others transformed into list of Series.
 439 |         """
 440 |         from pandas import (
 441 |             DataFrame,
 442 |             Series,
 443 |         )
 444 | 
 445 |         # self._orig is either Series or Index
 446 |         idx = self._orig if isinstance(self._orig, ABCIndex) else self._orig.index
 447 | 
 448 |         # Generally speaking, all objects without an index inherit the index
 449 |         # `idx` of the calling Series/Index - i.e. must have matching length.
 450 |         # Objects with an index (i.e. Series/Index/DataFrame) keep their own.
 451 |         if isinstance(others, ABCSeries):
 452 |             return [others]
 453 |         elif isinstance(others, ABCIndex):
 454 |             return [Series(others, index=idx, dtype=others.dtype)]
 455 |         elif isinstance(others, ABCDataFrame):
 456 |             return [others[x] for x in others]
 457 |         elif isinstance(others, np.ndarray) and others.ndim == 2:
 458 |             others = DataFrame(others, index=idx)
 459 |             return [others[x] for x in others]
 460 |         elif is_list_like(others, allow_sets=False):
 461 |             try:
 462 |                 others = list(others)  # ensure iterators do not get read twice etc
 463 |             except TypeError:
 464 |                 # e.g. ser.str, raise below
 465 |                 pass
 466 |             else:
 467 |                 # in case of list-like `others`, all elements must be
 468 |                 # either Series/Index/np.ndarray (1-dim)...
 469 |                 if all(
 470 |                     isinstance(x, (ABCSeries, ABCIndex, ExtensionArray))
 471 |                     or (isinstance(x, np.ndarray) and x.ndim == 1)
 472 |                     for x in others
 473 |                 ):
 474 |                     los: list[Series] = []
 475 |                     while others:  # iterate through list and append each element
 476 |                         los = los + self._get_series_list(others.pop(0))
 477 |                     return los
 478 |                 # ... or just strings
 479 |                 elif all(not is_list_like(x) for x in others):
 480 |                     return [Series(others, index=idx)]
 481 |         raise TypeError(
 482 |             "others must be Series, Index, DataFrame, np.ndarray "
 483 |             "or list-like (either containing only strings or "
 484 |             "containing only objects of type Series/Index/"
 485 |             "np.ndarray[1-dim])"
 486 |         )
